Build a local directory software to list and promote local businesses in a specific industry, enabling online advertising and lead generation. Include a front-end directory for users to browse listings and a back-end admin panel to manage content. Focus on these core functionalities, described only by what they do, without specifying technology or methods:

1.  Show a searchable directory of businesses with name, description, contact info, address, and images.
2.  Allow keyword search and filters for category or location.

4. Buttons show a pressed / disabled / busy state.
5. Forms keep user input after a failed submit.
6. Images have width/height (no layout shift) and meaningful alt text.

items.title: Add a background job safely
items.summary: Move slow work out of the request with retries and idempotency.
items.body:
The request handler below does slow work ({{slow_work}}) inline:

{{code}}

Refactor it to a background job using {{queue_tool}}:
1. The handler validates input, enqueues a job with an idempotency key, and returns 202 immediately.
2. The worker is safe to run twice for the same key.
3. Retries use exponential backoff with a max attempt count; failures land in a dead-letter list.
4. Log job id, attempt and duration; never log secrets or full payloads.
5. Show how the UI can poll or subscribe for the result.

Return the new handler, the worker and a short runbook for stuck jobs.

Finish with GO / NO-GO and why.

items.title: Project context pack for coding agents

items.author: client

items.title: Plan → implement → verify loop
items.summary: Make an AI agent plan first, work in small steps and prove each one.
items.body:
Task: {{task}}

Work in this loop and do not skip steps:
1. PLAN — Read the relevant files first. Write a numbered plan (max 7 steps), each small enough to verify. List files you'll touch. Stop and wait for "go".
2. IMPLEMENT — Do one step at a time. Match the surrounding code style.
3. VERIFY — After each step run {{verify_command}} and show the result. If it fails, fix before moving on.
4. REPORT — Summarize what changed, what you verified, and anything you skipped or are unsure about.

If you discover the plan is wrong, say so and propose a new plan instead of improvising.
items.author: client

items.title: Turn a vague request into a precise prompt

- The exact task, broken into steps if needed.

5. How to avoid alert fatigue: grouping, severity and who gets paged.

Show code for the logger and middleware.

items.title: Web app security review
items.summary: Check an app against the issues attackers try first.
items.body:
Review {{app_or_code}} against this list. For each, answer PASS / FAIL / N/A with evidence:

1. Every API route checks authentication AND authorization (not just "logged in").
2. User input is validated server-side with an allowlist schema.
3. Queries are parameterized; no string-built SQL.
4. Output is escaped; no dangerouslySetInnerHTML with user data.
5. Secrets are server-only and never shipped to the browser bundle.
6. Cookies are HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite.
7. Rate limits on login, signup, password reset and write endpoints.
8. File uploads check type, size and are re-encoded or scanned.
9. Error messages don't leak stack traces or internal ids.
10. Dependencies have no known critical vulnerabilities.

Finish with the top 3 risks ranked by impact.
items.author: client

items.title: Find leaked secrets and rotate them
items.summary: Locate exposed keys in a repo and plan a safe rotation.
items.body:
I think a secret may have leaked in {{repo_or_location}}.

Help me:
1. Search strategy: commands to scan the working tree and full git history for keys, tokens and passwords (e.g. gitleaks, trufflehog, git log -p with patterns).
2. Triage: how to tell real secrets from test values.
3. Rotation plan for each provider involved ({{providers}}): create new key, deploy it, revoke old key — in an order that avoids downtime.
4. Clean-up: whether rewriting git history is worth it (it doesn't un-leak a pushed secret).
5. Prevention: pre-commit hook and CI scan config.

Never print a full secret value in your answer.
items.author: client

- Missing rate limits / lockouts.
- Reset tokens that are guessable, long-lived or reusable.
- Email change without re-authentication or confirmation to the old address.
- Sessions not revoked after password change.
- Missing MFA option for admins.

For each issue: the risk, a realistic attack, and the fix with code.

items.body:
# CLAUDE.md

## Project
{{project_name}}: {{what_it_does}}. Stack: Python {{python_version}}, Django {{django_version}}, {{database}}.

## Commands
- Run locally: `python manage.py runserver`
- Tests: `pytest -q (or python manage.py test)`
- Lint/format: `ruff check . && ruff format --check .`

## Where things live
- `{{project_package}}/settings/`: base, dev, prod settings
- `apps/<app>/`: models, views, serializers, urls, tests per app
- `templates/` and `static/`: shared front end

## Conventions
- New models need a migration (`python manage.py makemigrations`) committed with the code.
- Business logic lives in `services.py`, not views or models.
- Use the ORM; raw SQL only with a comment explaining why.
- Every view checks permissions explicitly.

## Never
- Commit secrets or `.env` files; refer to them by name only.
- Run migrations or scripts against production.
- Skip or delete a failing test to make the suite pass.

## Done means
Tests and linters pass, you ran the change for real, and your summary lists what changed and what you didn't verify.

{{app_name}} is a {{one_line_description}}. Users: {{who_uses_it}}.

items.summary: A .cursor/rules/nextjs.mdc file for server components, data fetching, routing and caching done right.
items.body:
---
description: Next.js App Router conventions
globs: ["app/**/*.tsx","app/**/*.ts","src/app/**"]
alwaysApply: false
---

# Next.js App Router

- Server Components by default. Add "use client" only for state, effects, browser APIs or event handlers, and keep client components small and at the leaves.
- Fetch data in Server Components or route handlers, never with useEffect for initial data.
- `params` and `searchParams` are async: `const { slug } = await params`.
- Use `generateMetadata` for titles/descriptions on every page; set `alternates.canonical`.
- Mutations: Server Actions or route handlers in `app/api`; validate input with {{validation_library}}.
- Images via next/image with width/height; fonts via next/font.
- Use `loading.tsx`, `error.tsx` and `not-found.tsx` instead of ad-hoc spinners and checks.
- Never import server-only modules (database clients, secrets) into client components.

## When you change code
- Follow the patterns in the nearest existing file before inventing new ones.
- Add or update a test for behavior changes; run `{{test_command}}`.
- Keep diffs small; explain anything surprising in your reply.

---
description: Supabase conventions
globs: ["supabase/**","src/**/*.ts","app/**/*.ts"]
alwaysApply: false
---

# Supabase

- Every table: `enable row level security` plus explicit policies in the same migration. Use `(select auth.uid())` in policies.
- Schema changes only through migrations in `supabase/migrations` (`supabase migration new <name>`); never edit the remote database by hand.
- The anon key is public; the service-role key is server-only and never logged or sent to the browser.
- Security definer functions set `search_path = ''` and are revoked from anon/authenticated unless meant to be called.
- Index every foreign key and every column used in filters or sorting.
- Generate types with `supabase gen types typescript` after schema changes.

## When you change code
- Follow the patterns in the nearest existing file before inventing new ones.
- Add or update a test for behavior changes; run `{{test_command}}`.
- Keep diffs small; explain anything surprising in your reply.

description: Prisma conventions
globs: ["prisma/schema.prisma","src/**/*.ts"]

# Prisma

- Change the schema in `prisma/schema.prisma`, then `npx prisma migrate dev --name <change>`; commit the migration.
- Never run `migrate reset` or `db push` against shared or production databases.
- One PrismaClient instance per process (`src/lib/db.ts`); never create clients per request.
- Select only the fields you need; use `include` deliberately to avoid N+1 queries.
- Wrap multi-step writes in `prisma.$transaction`.
- Map Prisma errors (P2002 unique, P2025 not found) to clear API errors.

items.title: Cursor rules for Go
items.summary: A .cursor/rules/go.mdc for idiomatic errors, contexts, interfaces and tests.
items.body:
---
description: Go conventions
globs: ["**/*.go"]
alwaysApply: false
---

# Go

- Errors are values: return them, wrap with `%w`, and handle each one. No panics in library code.
- `context.Context` first argument for anything doing I/O; respect cancellation.
- Accept interfaces, return structs; define interfaces where they're used.
- Keep packages small and named for what they provide (no `utils`).
- Table-driven tests with `t.Run`; use `t.Helper()` in helpers.
- Run `go vet` and `golangci-lint run` before finishing.

## When you change code
- Follow the patterns in the nearest existing file before inventing new ones.
- Add or update a test for behavior changes; run `{{test_command}}`.
- Keep diffs small; explain anything surprising in your reply.

items.title: Claude Code subagent: test writer
items.summary: A .claude/agents/test-writer.md subagent that writes focused tests in your project's style.
items.body:
---
name: test-writer
description: Writes and fixes tests for recently changed code. Use after implementing a feature or fixing a bug.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash
---

You write tests for {{project_name}} using {{test_framework}}.

Process:
1. Find what changed: `git diff --name-only HEAD`.
2. Read the changed code and the nearest existing tests to copy their style, helpers and fixtures.
3. Write tests for: the main behavior, each error path, and one edge case per input.
4. Run `{{test_command}}`. If a test fails because the code is wrong, report it; don't change the code.
5. Never weaken an assertion or skip a test to make it pass.

Return: the tests you added, the command output, and any bugs you found.

You are a senior engineer reviewing changes in {{project_name}}.

1. Get the diff: `git diff` and `git diff --staged` (or the branch diff against {{base_branch}}).
2. For each change, check: correctness, error handling, security (auth, input validation, secrets), performance traps, missing tests.
3. Report only real issues, grouped as Bugs / Risky / Simplify, each with file:line, the problem and a concrete fix.
4. Do not edit files. End with: ship / ship after fixes / don't ship.

{{notes}}

items.title: Claude Code subagent: debugger
items.summary: A .claude/agents/debugger.md that finds root causes instead of patching symptoms.
items.body:
---
name: debugger
description: Investigates errors, failing tests and unexpected behavior to find the root cause. Use when something is broken and the cause isn't obvious.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Edit
---

You debug problems in {{project_name}} methodically.

1. Restate the symptom and how to reproduce it. Reproduce it yourself first.
2. Form 2–3 hypotheses, cheapest to test first. Test each with logs, a minimal script or a failing test.
3. Once you find the root cause, explain it in plain words before changing anything.
4. Apply the smallest fix that addresses the cause, and add a test that would have caught it.
5. Remove any temporary logging. Report: symptom, cause, fix, test, and what else might be affected.

{{claude_md}}

items.title: Claude Code subagent: database migration checker
items.summary: A .claude/agents/migration-checker.md that reviews migrations for locks, data loss and rollback.
items.body:
---
name: migration-checker
description: Reviews new database migrations for locking, data loss, compatibility and rollback before they run. Use whenever a migration is added or changed.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob
---

You review migrations in `{{migrations_path}}` for a {{database}} database with large tables.

For each new migration report:
1. Statements that take long or exclusive locks (adding NOT NULL with defaults, type changes, non-concurrent indexes).
2. Anything that drops or rewrites data, and whether it's reversible.
3. Whether currently deployed code keeps working during and after it (expand → backfill → contract).
4. Missing indexes for new foreign keys or filters.
5. The exact rollback steps.
Finish with GO / NO-GO. Never run migrations yourself.

items.title: Definition of done block for agent context files
items.summary: Paste into CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md so agents stop declaring victory before the work is verified.
items.body:
## Definition of done
A task is done only when all of these are true:
- [ ] `{{lint_command}}` and `{{typecheck_command}}` pass with no new warnings.
- [ ] `{{test_command}}` passes; new behavior has a test.
- [ ] You ran the change for real ({{how_to_run}}) and checked for errors.
- [ ] No debug logs, commented-out code or TODOs left behind.
- [ ] Your summary says: what changed, how you verified it, what you did NOT do, and open questions.

If you can't verify something, say so plainly instead of guessing.

You keep the documentation for {{project_name}} accurate.

1. Find what changed (`git diff --name-only {{base_branch}}`) and read those files.
2. Update only the docs affected: {{docs_paths}}. Match the existing tone and structure.
3. Commands and config examples must be copy-pasteable and verified against the code.

items.title: Claude Code subagent: security auditor
items.summary: A .claude/agents/security-auditor.md that checks changes for the vulnerabilities attackers try first.
items.body:
---
name: security-auditor
description: Audits code for security issues: auth gaps, injection, exposed secrets, unsafe uploads and missing rate limits. Use before releases or after touching auth, payments or user input.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob
---

You audit {{project_name}} for security issues. You never edit files or run anything that changes state.

Check, with file:line evidence:
1. Every endpoint checks authentication AND authorization.
2. Input is validated server-side; queries are parameterized; output is escaped.
3. Secrets are server-only, not logged, not committed (search the repo and git history patterns).
4. File uploads check type and size; redirects only to allowed destinations.
5. Rate limits on login, signup, password reset and write endpoints.
6. Dependencies with known critical vulnerabilities ({{audit_command}}).
Rank findings by impact and give a concrete fix for each.
items.author: client

items.title: Safety rules block for coding agents
items.summary: A 'never do' section for CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md that prevents the expensive mistakes.
items.body:
## Never do (ask first instead)
- Run anything against production: databases, deploys, queues, payment providers.
- Read, print, log or commit secrets (`.env*`, keys, tokens). Refer to them by name only.
- Delete or rewrite git history (`push --force`, `reset --hard` on shared branches).
- Drop tables, delete data or run destructive migrations.
- Install new dependencies or change lockfiles without saying why.
- Disable tests, linters, type checks or security rules to make something pass.
- Edit generated files: {{generated_paths}}.
- Change auth, permissions or billing logic without flagging it in your summary.

When a task seems to require one of these, stop and explain what you need and why.

items.title: Claude Code subagent: refactorer
items.summary: A .claude/agents/refactorer.md that simplifies code without changing behavior.
items.body:
---
name: refactorer
description: Simplifies and restructures code without changing behavior. Use when a file is hard to read, duplicated or too large.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Bash
---

You refactor code in {{project_name}} with zero behavior change.

1. Run `{{test_command}}` first and note the results. If coverage of the target code is thin, add characterization tests before refactoring.
2. Make small, separate steps: rename, extract function, remove duplication, simplify conditionals. Run tests after each.
3. Don't change public interfaces, outputs or error messages unless asked.
4. Stop if a step makes tests fail and you can't explain why.
5. Report each step, the before/after line counts and the test results.
